# Example Crossing Context

Bounded Context view of `example-crossing-context`, release 3. Generated by `scripts/generate.sh`; never hand-edited.

The context a team needs when its workflows span the agency and the platform office.

Written for: Engineers and analysts who work across both organizations.

## Organizations

- `example-agency`
- `example-platform`

## Upstream documents

- `example-agency` — recorded release 1, now at release 1, at `file:documents/org/example-agency.yaml`.
- `example-platform` — recorded release 4, now at release 4, at `url:https://code.example.invalid/example-platform/documents/org/example-platform.yaml`. Currency not verified: the copy was read through a local override, so its release is asserted rather than checked.

## Source selection

- `intake-counts` — preferred: The claims warehouse read API. It is the only source whose counts the owning team will stand behind.
- `intake-counts-spreadsheet` — rejected: A spreadsheet an operator maintains by hand. Nobody owns it, and two readers have already found different numbers in it.

## Discovery index

- `example-agency#claims-warehouse` — Claims Warehouse (data-warehouse, active); interfaces: `read-api` (rest).
- `example-platform#context-server` — Example Context Server (mcp-server, active); interfaces: `admin-api` (rest), `hosted` (mcp).
- `example-crossing-context#legacy-extract` — Legacy Nightly Extract (service, deprecated); interfaces: .

Host-tool authentication: A tool already signed in on this machine, such as a forge CLI or a cloud SDK, carries the credential.

## Outputs

- Roles: `analyst`, `engineer`
- Guidance: Start from the view; it says which of the two organizations owns each fact.
- Destination: `file:views/example-crossing-context`

## Limitations

- The platform office's release cadence is faster than this document's, so a reference can be a release behind for a week.

## Access failures

- example-platform#context-server — Requested a session through the platform office's access form. Pending since the last release; the system stays not-established until it clears.
